title: Native colour input across required system webviews

cases.session: macOS 15 hosted desktop session; WKWebView; runner macos-15
setup: Use only the synthetic S10 page, with the initial committed value #336699. The native runner must drive the app and picker; it must not set input.value or synthesize a native selection through page script.
Capture environment.json details and start whole desktop, compositor, simulator or emulator recording before the first interaction.
actions: Launch the named desktop or test-shell-mobile wrapper with pages/colour/ in its real system webview. Record the exact OS, session, display, SDK/runtime and webview versions before input.
Open the Appearance dialog by visible native click/tap. Activate the labelled Custom colour picker by native click/tap and capture its native tree and whole-screen picker chrome.

On desktop, exercise keyboard navigation and acceptance in native picker controls where exposed. On mobile, operate the native picker by touch and enter HEX using the on-screen keyboard. Record the input route and focus return.
Choose a first non-default colour using native picker controls and accept it. Record the exact returned value and input/change events. Apply the Appearance draft and record the committed value.

Reopen the dialog, choose and accept a distinct second non-default colour through native picker controls, then cancel the Appearance dialog. Reopen once more, test manual HEX #E0A526 and short HEX abc, then invalid #12XZ; cancel each uncommitted edit.

Reopen the Appearance dialog, open the native picker, and exercise every supported cancel, Escape, close, Back or outside-dismissal route. Record each route used, whole-screen capture, native tree and focus returned to the webview.

assertions.requirement: The labelled input opens an observable, usable native colour picker through real input. Record the per-cell planning verdict as native picker usable, hex field only, or UNVERIFIED.
assertions.expected: native picker usable only when native chrome and controls are visible and operable; otherwise record the observed limitation as hex field only. Missing runner, session, native tree or full capture is UNVERIFIED with conservative hex-only selection, never an empirical broken-picker claim.

assertions.requirement: Two distinct non-default colours chosen in native picker controls are accepted and returned to the webview; focus return is observable.
assertions.expected: Each returned value matches ^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$, is normalized to lowercase at the page boundary, and matches the Draft output and event log. The page receives focus after picker acceptance. Picker interaction is native and never a programmatic value assignment.

assertions.requirement: The Appearance model commits Apply and discards Cancel independently of native picker acceptance.
assertions.expected: Apply commits the first accepted native colour exactly. After reopening, accepting a different second native colour and cancelling the Appearance dialog leaves the committed value byte-for-byte unchanged.

assertions.requirement: Manual HEX entry, invalid input, exact custom-colour retention and the under-3:1 warning are usable in this webview.
assertions.expected: #E0A526 is accepted and normalized to #e0a526; the warning reports a light or dark theme ratio below 3:1 without changing the value. abc normalizes to #aabbcc. Invalid #12XZ exposes an accessible error and does not alter the current draft or committed Appearance value.

assertions.requirement: Keyboard or touch interaction is usable in the platform's native picker presentation and the HEX fallback.
assertions.expected: The picker opens with a real click; native controls are operable with keyboard navigation and keyboard acceptance where exposed; focus returns to the labelled input.

assertions.requirement: Supported native-picker dismissal routes leave values unchanged and return interaction to the webview.
assertions.expected: Record every native dismissal route exposed by this picker. Dismissing without acceptance leaves both draft and committed Appearance values unchanged and returns focus to the webview. A route absent from the native UI is reported as unsupported, not passed.
